newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends mostly up despite weak CBOT soyoil.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends mostly up despite weak CBOT soyoil.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed mostly higher on crusher-related commercial buying but gains were tempered by weakness in CBOT soyoil and continued hedge selling, floor sources said.
They also noted concern that continued strength in the Canadian dollar could have had an adverse impact of exports.
Trade was active for the third consecutive day. March canola closed $0.50 higher at $412.20.
Flaxseed was slightly lower as a few hedge-related sell orders helped reverse an early advance which had been driven by export-related commercial buying.
Western barley futures finished higher supported by commission house buying and spillover strength from gains in CBOT corn. February closed $1.50 higher at $137.50.
Wheat futures were aided by strength in other feed grain markets with Cargill a featured buyer. Moderate hedge selling limited gains and March closed just $0.80 up at $171.50.
Feed peas and oats saw light commercial bidding but remained tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
